text:
Although well over half of the population in the Oconee and Pickens County area is rural, agriculture is relatively insignificant in the local economy, accounting for only 1.68 percent of the total workforce and less than 1 percent of earnings.
Personal income in Oconee County in 1972 totaled $167.2 million. Per capita personal income was $3,913 in the same year, 87 percent of the national average. By comparison in 1950, Oconee County's per capita personal income was only 45 percent of the national average. Personal income for Pickens County in 1972 totaled about $177.4 million (calculation from Regional Economics Information System, Bureau of Economic Analysis). Per capita personal income for the Greenville-Spartanburg SMSA, of which Pickens is a part, was $3,819 in 1972 or 85 percent of the national average. Separate data for Pickens County are not available, in some cases due to its inclusion in the Greenville-Spartanburg, SMSA (Table 2-17).
In 1970, the percent of Oconee and Pickens workforce unemployed was 2.5 percent and 2.1 percent respectively, which was lower than for the State as a whole (Table 2-18). As of February 1975, however, the numbers of unemployed increased to approximately 8 percent for Oconee County and 16 percent for Pickens. Most of this unemployment arose from layoffs in the textile industry. (Source: Telephone conversations, 2/21/75, with Oconee County Planning Commission and Pickens County Employment Security Commission).
The tax rate for Oconee County where the project would be constructed is 139 mills based on a 3.5 percent assessed valuation. The county offers new industry a 5-year abatement period during which only the school tax rate of 98 mills would be in effect.
Oconee County has 5 high schools, 4 junior high schools, 14 elementary schools, and 7 kindergartens. Student enrollment in all schools, kindergarten classes through 12th grade, was 10,305 in May 1974. The Pickens County Public School System includes 4 high schools, 4 junior high schools, 18 elementary schools and 5 kindergartens. The 1972-1973 enrollment was 13,410.
In 1963 Oconee, Pickens, and Anderson Counties cosponsored construction of the Tri-county Technical Education Center for post-high school technical education.
